body:
Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective January 1, 2022

Policy No. CS:33.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 1 High Risk Referrals Purpose To ensure that high risk participants are identified and referred appropriately to a health care provider (HCP), Registered Dietitian (RD), or International Board Certified Lactation Consultant (IBCLC). Authority 7 CFR Part 246.7 Policy Local Agencies (LAs) must follow the State Agency High Risk policy that identifies the high-risk conditions requiring referral and the required follow- up documentation of the referrals. Each Local Agency (LA) must develop a local agency specific High Risk policy that outlines their LA’s procedures for follow-up, any additional high risk criteria beyond those specified in this policy, and their written procedures for responding to Red Flags criteria. Definitions Health care provider (HCP): Also referred to as “prescriptive authority”; a medical professional who may legally diagnose medical conditions and write prescriptions. In Texas, prescriptive authorities include but are not limited to medical doctors (MD), doctors of osteopathy (DO), physician’s assistants (PA/PA-C), and nurse practitioners (NP). Registered dietitian (RD): A credentialed nutrition professional authorized to provide management of health and diet concerns. International Board Certified Lactation Consultant (IBCLC): A credentialed lactation professional authorized to provide clinical management of breastfeeding concerns.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective January 1, 2022

Policy No. CS:33.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 2 Follow-up: A. Internal – Efforts the LA WIC professional makes to complete the referral. B. External - Efforts the LA makes to contact the participant and determine the outcome (disposition) of the referral. Internal referrals: Referrals made to a professional within WIC (i.e., local agency RD or IBCLC). External referrals: Referrals made to a professional outside of WIC (e.g., health care provider or emergency room). Procedures I. High risk conditions and corresponding categorical groups requiring referral to internal and external sources. A. The following minimum risk criteria for internal referrals are: 1. RD a. Formula fed infants: FTT (RC 134), Slowed/Faltering Growth Pattern – infants 2 weeks of age or less with excessive weight loss of ≥7% birth weight (RC 135), Underweight – infant (RC 103A), Very Low Birth Weight (RC 141B) b. Children: FTT (RC 134), Very Low Birth Weight – children <24 months of age (RC 141B) c. Pregnant women: Low Maternal Weight Gain During Pregnancy – during 2nd or 3rd trimester for singleton pregnancy (RC 131) 2. IBCLC a. Pregnant women: Breastfeeding Complications or Potential Complications (RC 602) b. Breastfeeding women: Breastfeeding Complications or Potential Complications (RC 602)

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective January 1, 2022

Policy No. CS:33.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 3 c. Breastfed Infants: FTT (RC 134), Slowed/Faltering Growth Pattern – infants 2 weeks of age or less with excessive weight loss of ≥7% birth weight (RC 135), Underweight – infant (RC 103A), Very Low Birth Weight (RC 141B), Breastfeeding Complications or Potential Complications (RC 603) 3. Infants that are both formula and breastfed can be referred to a RD and/or IBCLC. B. The following minimum risk criteria for external referrals are: 1. HCP a. All Infants: Slowed/Faltering Growth Pattern – infants 2 weeks of age or less with excessive weight loss of ≥7% birth weight (RC 135) C. The following minimum risk criteria for internal and/or external referrals are below. Professional judgement should be used to determine which of the following health care professionals the referral should be made to. 1. HCP and/or RD a. Pregnant women: Gestational Diabetes (RC 302), Nutrient Deficiency Diseases (RC 341), Gastrointestinal Disorders (RC 342), Diabetes Mellitus (RC 343), Hypertension (RC 345A), Prehypertension (RC 345B), Renal Disease (RC 346), Cancer (RC 347), Central Nervous System Disorders (RC 348), Genetic and Congenital Disorders (RC 349), Inborn Errors of Metabolism (RC 351), Celiac Disease (RC 354), Eating Disorders (RC 358), Developmental, Sensory, or Motor Disabilities Interfering with the Ability to Eat (RC 362) b. Breastfeeding women: Nutrient Deficiency Diseases (RC 341), Gastrointestinal Disorders (RC 342), Diabetes Mellitus (RC 343), Hypertension (RC 345A), Prehypertension (RC 345B), Renal Disease (RC 346), Cancer (RC 347), Central Nervous System Disorders (RC

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective January 1, 2022

Policy No. CS:33.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 4 348), Genetic and Congenital Disorders (RC 349), Inborn Errors of Metabolism (RC 351), Celiac Disease (RC 354), Eating Disorders (RC 358), Developmental, Sensory, or Motor Disabilities Interfering with the Ability to Eat (RC 362) c. Postpartum women: Nutrient Deficiency Diseases (RC 341), Gastrointestinal Disorders (RC 342), Diabetes Mellitus (RC 343), Hypertension (RC 345A), Prehypertension (RC 345B), Renal Disease (RC 346), Cancer (RC 347), Central Nervous System Disorders (RC 348), Genetic and Congenital Disorders (RC 349), Inborn Errors of Metabolism (RC 351), Celiac Disease (RC 354), Eating Disorders (RC 358), Developmental, Sensory, or Motor Disabilities Interfering with the Ability to Eat (RC 362) d. All Infants: Nutrient Deficiency Diseases (RC 341), Gastrointestinal Disorders (RC 342), Diabetes Mellitus (RC 343), Hypertension (RC 345A), Prehypertension (RC 345B), Renal Disease (RC 346), Cancer (RC 347), Central Nervous System Disorders (RC 348), Genetic and Congenital Disorders (RC 349), Inborn Errors of Metabolism (RC 351), Celiac Disease (RC 354), Developmental, Sensory, or Motor Disabilities Interfering with the Ability to Eat (RC 362) e. Children: Nutrient Deficiency Diseases (RC 341), Gastrointestinal Disorders (RC 342), Diabetes Mellitus (RC 343), Hypertension (RC 345A), Prehypertension (RC 345B), Renal Disease (RC 346), Cancer (RC 347), Central Nervous System Disorders (RC 348), Genetic and Congenital Disorders (RC 349), Inborn Errors of Metabolism (RC 351), Celiac Disease (RC 354), Developmental, Sensory, or Motor Disabilities Interfering with the Ability to Eat (RC 362)

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective January 1, 2022

Policy No. CS:33.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 5 D. In the event that a participant is already under the care of an external RD, IBCLC, or HCP for the high risk condition, a referral may not be warranted. This must be documented in the participant’s record. E. Additional high risk criteria beyond those specified in this policy must be clearly defined in each LA’s local agency High Risk policy. II. Procedures for follow-up A. The LA specific developed policy for RD, IBCLC, and HCP referrals must include the following: 1. Method of follow-up to be used with participant (e.g., phone, appointment) 2. Length of time between referral and follow-up that is measurable (e.g., 1 month, 7 days) B. State Agency required documentation of follow-up must be in the following areas of the MIS record: 1. All Internal and External Referrals a. On the Pending High Risk Referral page complete the following fields: i. Follow-up Details ii. Follow-up Completion Details 2. RD a. Internal: Goals and/or Notes Section of VENA Documentation Page b. External: Goals and/or Notes Section of VENA Documentation Page 3. IBCLC a. Internal: Goals and/or Notes Section of VENA Documentation Page b. External: Goals and/or Notes Section of VENA Documentation Page 4. HCP a. External: Goals and/or Notes Section of VENA Documentation Page

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective January 1, 2022

Policy No. CS:33.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 6 III. For external referrals, the LA must obtain the participant’s consent before contacting the health care provider to which a participant was referred to determine disposition (outcome) of referral. IV. Per policy GA:14.0 Staffing Standards, LAs that do not have an RD or IBCLC must request a waiver and have a written contingency plan for providing referrals and high risk individual counseling while position is vacant. V. LAs that do not have an IBCLC on staff, or access to a community IBCLC who provides services free of charge to WIC participants, must access an IBCLC via a WIC Lactation Support Center who can provide phone or virtual consultation. VI. Participants who have been identified as having Red Flag criteria must immediately be referred to receive medical care. The place or service that a participant will be referred must be specified in a LA specific high risk policy (e.g., urgent care center, emergency room, 911). A. Red Flags: 1. Infant a. Skin color is blue or gray b. Skin color is yellow. This is a medical emergency if the infant is not under the care of a HCP and/or showing signs of lethargy, fever, and poor feeding. c. Poor hydration as indicated by a combination of the following: i. soft spot(s) on top of head sunken in ii. skin on the back of infant’s hand, forearm or belly lightly pinched between the thumb and forefinger for a few seconds does not return to normal contour within three seconds iii. sunken eyes iv. no tears or few tears when crying v. extremely dry lips, mouth or tongue vi. lethargy

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective January 1, 2022

Policy No. CS:33.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 7 vii. Signs of trauma or bruising viii. Difficult or shallow breathing, wheezing 2. Child a. Signs of trauma or bruising b. Difficult or shallow breathing, wheezing c. Poor hydration as indicated by a combination of the following: i. skin on the back of child’s hand, forearm or belly lightly pinched between the thumb and forefinger for a few seconds does not return to normal contour within three seconds ii. sunken eyes iii. no tears or few tears when crying iv. extremely dry lips, mouth or tongue v. scant, dark, or foul-smelling urine vi. lethargy 3. Pregnant a. Signs of labor initiation – regular contractions, leaking/gushing fluid from vagina b. Heavy bleeding from vagina at any time of pregnancy c. Injury - accident/fall/blow to the belly d. Observed at clinic under the influence of alcohol or drugs/narcotics with risk of potential harm to self or others 4. Breastfeeding, Postpartum a. Hearing voices or seeing things that are not real or having false beliefs (delusions) b. Observed at clinic under the influence of alcohol or drugs/narcotics with risk of potential harm to self or others c. Postpartum Mood Disorder Signs: i. Thoughts of harming self or baby ii. High level of anxiety iii. Flat affect iv. Not making eye contact with baby/not responding to infant cries/ not enjoying baby v. No appetite/ inability to sleep

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective January 1, 2022

Policy No. CS:33.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 8 5. WIC staff must not diagnose or provide medical advice to participants. Guidelines A. The criteria in this policy are minimum criteria, and LAs are encouraged to include additional criteria relevant to their local population and concerns. Participants who desire a consultation for any reason outside of these criteria must be referred to the appropriate professional. B. There are examples of conditions in the High Risk Referral Guidelines section located in the Clinic Assessment Manual to assist LAs in developing their local policy. If desired, LAs can select from these criteria based on the needs of their local agency and clientele. The guidelines are a resource that represents suggestions for high risk referrals. However, local agencies are not required nor limited to use any or all of the criteria on the list.
citation_label: Texas WIC Policy and Procedures Manual CS:33.0 High Risk Referrals 1

body:
Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective July 1, 2026 Policy No. CS:35.0

CS:35.0 – Certification of Homeless and Those Living in Shelters and Institutions 1 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

Certification of Homeless and Those Living in Shelters and Institutions Purpose To ensure the eligible homeless applicants have access to WIC services. WIC services must benefit the WIC participant and not the homeless facility, as required by federal regulation. Authority CFR 246.7 Policy The local agency (LA) staff must check the identification, income, and residency of each applicant/participant and parent/guardian applying on behalf of an infant and/or child at each certification. The LA must establish to the extent possible that shelter/institution/homeless facility where participants reside meets the conditions in this policy. Definitions Residency – The location or address where applicant routinely lives or spends the night. Homeless Individual – A woman, infant, or child who lacks a fixed and regular nighttime residence; or whose primary nighttime residence is: ● a supervised publicly or privately operated shelter (including a welfare hotel, a congregate shelter, or a shelter for victims of domestic violence) designated to provide temporary living accommodation; ● an institution that provides a temporary residence for individuals intended to be institutionalized; ● a temporary accommodation in the residence of another individual not exceeding 365 days;

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective July 1, 2026 Policy No. CS:35.0

CS:35.0 – Certification of Homeless and Those Living in Shelters and Institutions 2 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

● a public or private place not designated for, or ordinarily used as, a regular sleeping accommodation for human beings, including those residing in vehicles, parks, hallways, doorsteps, vacant buildings, etc. Homeless Facility – The following types of facilities which provide meal service: ● a supervised publicly or privately-operated shelter (including a welfare hotel or congregate shelter) designed to provide temporary living accommodations; ● a facility that provides a temporary residence for individuals intended to be institutionalized; or ● a public or private place not designed for, nor normally used as, a regular sleeping accommodation for human beings. Institution – Any residential accommodation which provides meal service, except private residences and homeless facilities. Procedures I. Enrolling homeless persons or those living in shelters or institutions: A. Identification - applicants must provide proof of identification with: 1. acceptable proof as outlined in CS:05.0 Identification of a WIC Applicant/Participant and Parent or Guardian, or 2. a WIC Self- Declaration Form for Identification, Residency, Zero- Income (Cash on Hand) and Proof of Income (Homeless) if no proof of identification exists (SKU:13-06-13567). A copy or electronic image of the form must be scanned and uploaded to the MIS. Documents obtained via electronic transmission are automatically saved in the MIS. B. Residency – applicants must provide proof of residency with one of the following: 1. acceptable proof as outlined in CS:06.0 Residency as a Certification Requirement, or

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective July 1, 2026 Policy No. CS:35.0

CS:35.0 – Certification of Homeless and Those Living in Shelters and Institutions 3 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

2. signed statement from shelter verifying residency, or 3. a WIC Self-Declaration Form (SKU:13-06-13567) if no proof exists. A copy or electronic image of the form must be scanned and uploaded to the MIS. Documents obtained via electronic transmission are automatically saved in the MIS. C. Income – Applicant must provide proof of income with one of the following: 1. acceptable proof, as outlined in CS:07.0 Income Screening as a Certification Requirement, or 2. a WIC Self-Declaration Form (SKU:13-06-13567) if no proof exists. A copy or electronic image of the form must be scanned and uploaded to the MIS. Documents obtained via electronic transmission are automatically saved in the MIS. II. Shelter/Institution/Homeless Facility Requirements and Documentation Where the Families Currently Reside A. Requirements – The LA must evaluate whether the shelter/institution/homeless facility meets the following conditions: 1. it does not accrue financial or in-kind benefit from the applicant's participation in WIC, and 2. WIC foods must not be used in communal feedings, but are available exclusively to the WIC participant for whom they were issued; and 3. it does not place constraints on the ability of the applicant to partake of the WIC food benefits and all associated WIC services. B. The LA must ensure that the shelter/institution/homeless facility meets the requirements by: 1. contacting all facilities every three years where WIC participants currently reside to verify the required conditions are being met.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective July 1, 2026 Policy No. CS:35.0

CS:35.0 – Certification of Homeless and Those Living in Shelters and Institutions 4 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

The contact may be via phone, email or signed letter of agreement from the facility. 2. retaining the documentation of contact or attempt to contact the facility for audit/review. 3. requesting the facility notify the LA if any of the conditional requirements are no longer being met. III. Non-compliant Shelters/Institution/Homeless Facility A. When a facility is determined to be noncompliant to conditional requirements, the LA must: 1. Refer participants to alternate facilities inside the LAs service area that meet compliance requirements. 2. If the participants do not want to reside in the alternate facility continue issuing food benefits and services and inform the participants that their WIC food benefits will discontinue at the end of their certification period if they continue to reside in a noncompliant facility, with the exception of infants. Certified infants must continue to receive all their food benefits regardless of their residence. 3. Continue to provide other WIC services to all participants residing in the facility, such as nutrition education, breastfeeding promotion and support, and health care referral services. B. In situations where there are no alternate compliant shelters available, continue to certify and provide food benefits to eligible participants residing in a noncompliant shelter. IV. If shelter/homeless facility/institution does not receive physical mail, proxies of participants residing in these facilities may pick up assigned Texas WIC Card(s) for the endorser and redeem food benefits in bulk for multiple participants residing in the facility. The LA must ensure that adult participants are allowed to participate in the process of picking up their Texas WIC Card and shopping for their food benefits to the

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective July 1, 2026 Policy No. CS:35.0

CS:35.0 – Certification of Homeless and Those Living in Shelters and Institutions 5 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

greatest extent possible, within the homeless facility/institutional framework, so that they are aware of the foods prescribed for them as well as the intended benefits of such foods. Guidelines Informing participants of the shelter/institution/homeless facility requirements will help to ensure that conditions continue to be met.

body:
Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. CS:36.0(eWIC)

CS:36.0(eWIC) - Process for Mailing the Texas WIC Card WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 1 Process for Mailing the Texas WIC Card Purpose To provide Local Agencies (LAs) guidance on the process for mailing Texas WIC Cards. Authority 7 CFR Part 246.4; 246.7; 246.12 Policy LAs may mail Texas WIC Cards to each economic unit that requests the Texas WIC Card be mailed, or under the following circumstances: • Reasons as outlined in Policy CS:04.0 (T): Physical Presence • Lack of transportation and inability to reschedule during the issuance month • National or State declared Emergencies, Disasters, or Public Health Emergencies, such as a pandemic or natural disaster Definitions Assign Texas WIC Card – The process of assigning the Texas WIC Card to an economic unit. Economic Unit – All persons, related and/or unrelated, living together in the same dwelling, except for the following special situations: pregnant woman, infants/children placed through Department of Family Protective Services (DFPFS); e.g., foster/kinship, and individuals who qualify as a separate economic unit. Electronic Benefit Account (EBA) – The account where food benefits are being held for redemption. EBT Processor – The vendor responsible for mailing the Texas WIC Card, when requested through myWIC and the WIC Card Management Line.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. CS:36.0(eWIC)

CS:36.0(eWIC) - Process for Mailing the Texas WIC Card WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 2 WIC Card Management Line – An interactive voice response system where clients can manage the Texas WIC Card (set/reset the PIN, cancel/replace the card), obtain food benefit balances, and speak to customer service associate. WIC Card Mailer – The document included with the mailed Texas WIC Cards that provides participants with important information, including a QR code to the required documents that must be given at initial certification or recertification appointments. Procedures I. Once benefits have been uploaded to the economic unit’s EBA, a client may request to have the Texas WIC Card mailed. To complete this process, staff must: A. Verify the Endorser's name, date of birth, and zip code. Verify and/or update the current mailing address. B. Offer the following mailing options: 1. Mailed from EBT processor 2. Mailed from the clinic. If mailed from the clinic, staff must ensure the following: a. The card must be mailed within 1 business day. b. Mail the card with the Texas WIC Card Mailer. (Card mailer includes QR codes to all required documents listed in CR:01, effective April 1, 2026). c. The envelope must specify “do not forward, return to sender”. C. Document appropriate mailing method in the MIS. D. Staff must inform the client that a PIN must be set prior to shopping at the grocery store and it may be set via myWIC or WIC Card Management Line. II. When the Texas WIC Card is not received via mail, staff must check MIS for any redemptions of current month benefits.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. CS:36.0(eWIC)

CS:36.0(eWIC) - Process for Mailing the Texas WIC Card WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 3 A. If redemptions have not been made: 1. Verify mailing address with participant and update if needed. 2. Repeat steps in Procedure I. above if client is not physically present. B. If redemptions have been made: 1. Verify mailing address with participant. 2. Verify with the participant whether any other household members have set the PIN and redeemed benefits. 3. If LA staff verify the redeemed benefits were not made by the client or anyone in the household, follow the procedures in WIC Policy CS:26.0 (effective April 1, 2026) for replacing the Texas WIC Card and complete the online form WIC Vendor Complaint and Client Dispute Form to gather information from the client and conduct research. C. If a card is not delivered to the client and returned to the clinic, staff must contact the client to confirm the correct address. 1. If the delivery address is incorrect, update the MIS with the correct address. 2. Mail the Texas WIC Card to the correct address following the steps in Procedure I.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 1

Effective: December 1, 2017 Policy FD: 02.0 (T)

Frequency of Issuance of Food Benefits

Purpose To provide a uniform procedure for issuing WIC benefits to participants, ensuring adequate nutrition education (NE) opportunities, and preserving coordination with other health services such as immunizations and prenatal care. Authority 7 CFR Part 246.12 Policy Local agencies (LAs) shall implement a benefits issuance/nutrition education routine for all participants that meets the educational and follow-up needs of the participant not to exceed each participant's total food entitlement within his/her certification period. No more than three months of food benefits can be issued at one time. The Texas WIC Card may hold the current month’s issuance plus the next 3 month’s issuance. Food for all participants within the family will be aggregated on the card.

Procedures I. LAs shall meet the minimum federal requirements of two NE contacts within a certification period.

II. The Certifying Authority shall determine individual participants who would benefit from frequent NE contacts such as, pregnant women who enter WIC late in pregnancy or individuals with high risk conditions who require individual nutrition counseling and adjust the issuance length accordingly.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 2

Effective: December 1, 2017 Policy FD: 02.0 (T)

III. If a family member's certification expires during the current month, but the family member is eligible for subsequent certification, the system will advance issue a single month’s benefits to other family members after the month certification expires. If the family member is subsequently certified for the following month, up to three months’ issuance will resume. If any family member becomes categorically ineligible (woman attaining six month postpartum or one year breastfeeding or child turning five years old), the other family members shall still receive full advance issuance.

IV. When participants fail to pick up benefits: A. The MIS will automatically inactivate participants who fail to pick up benefits for two (2) consecutive months. B. LAs shall reactivate, if caseload permits, participants who return before their certification period expires. C. If the participant fails to return for subsequent certification, then the record will be automatically terminated for Failure to Subcertify

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective July 1, 2026 Policy No. FD:03.0

FD:03.0 – Designating a Proxy 1 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

Designating a Proxy Purpose Provide guidance to Local Agency staff on how a participant/parent/guardian/caretaker may designate a proxy. Authority 7 CFR Part 246.12; 26 TAC Section 366.5 Policy A participant/parent/guardian/caretaker may designate a proxy in writing for up to 3 months. The proxy must be entered into the MIS. Definitions Caretaker – any person, 18 years of age or older, designated by a woman participant, parent, or guardian, to obtain and transact benefits. A caretaker is appointed as a benefit recipient and has custodial responsibility for a participant during most of their time awake each day. Proxy – any person 16 years of age or older, designated by a woman participant, parent, guardian or caretaker of an infant or child participant, to obtain and transact benefits. The proxy must be entered into the MIS. Procedures I. A participant/parent/guardian/caretaker may designate a proxy when unable to come to the clinic in circumstances where in-person attendance may be required A. Circumstances that may require in-person attendance include but are not limited to: 1. Receiving Nutrition Education. (Refer to policy NE:01.0). 2. Obtaining an assigned and/or replaced Texas WIC Card.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective July 1, 2026 Policy No. FD:03.0

FD:03.0 – Designating a Proxy 2 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

3. Obtaining and returning a breast pump. (Refer to policy BF:07.0). 4. Obtaining a special formula that has been shipped to the clinic. (Refer to policy FD:18.0). B. A proxy must be designated in writing by the participant/parent/ guardian/caretaker when in-person attendance is required. The written statement is valid up to 3 months, and must include: 1. Proxy name; 2. Date statement was written (must be current, within 30 days); and 3. The participant/parent/guardian/caretaker signature. C. If the proxy brings the written statement to the in-person appointment, staff must upload to the MIS. Written statements obtained via electronic transmission will automatically be uploaded and saved to the MIS. D. If a proxy is selected, staff will enter the start date and end date that the proxy designation is valid into the MIS. E. The proxy must provide identification for himself/herself. (Refer to policy CS:05.0). II. Individuals unable to write may make their mark in lieu of a signature on the written statement. A. LA staff may assist clients who cannot write with preparation of the written statement; however, another staff member must witness. This option is more helpful to the family if completed at the clinic in advance of a future appointment when it is known the participant/parent/guardian/caretaker will need a proxy. B. A third party other than LA staff may also assist the participant/ parent/guardian/caretaker in preparation of the written statement.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective July 1, 2026 Policy No. FD:03.0

FD:03.0 – Designating a Proxy 3 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

Examples of a third party include but are not limited to family members and friends. III. Refer to policy CS:35.0 for a proxy appointed by a participant residing in a shelter/homeless facility/institution. IV. In certain circumstances, a proxy may be appointed by the state agency. The state agency will work with the LA to approve a designation of a proxy to obtain benefits for an infant, child, or other participant under age 18 who is subject to disqualification but who would be at health risk, including nutritional risk, if benefits were terminated. V. LA employees may not be designated as proxies.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective: April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:06.0

FD:06.0 - Texas WIC Card Management WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 1 Texas WIC Card Management Purpose To ensure proper accountability for WIC Lone Star cards assigned to the Local Agency (LA) and/or clinic prior to issuance. Authority 7 CFR Part 246.12

Policy The State Agency (SA) will order Texas WIC cards for each Local Agency (LA) from the EBT Vendor and conduct a monthly assessment to ensure the card supply is maintained. The LA administrative site must report to the State Agency (SA) when all Texas WIC Card bulk inventory shipments are received and provide accounts of the amount received. The LA administrative site must report any discrepancies in Texas WIC Cards during the internal LA clinic distribution process. Definitions EBT Vendor - The vendor who mails Texas WIC Cards to each LA administrative site. Procedures I. Texas WIC Card Supply A. The SA will order Texas WIC Cards through the EBT Vendor for all LAs and enter the number of cards into each clinic’s card inventory in the MIS. B. The SA will conduct a monthly assessment of each LA and Clinic Site card inventory and will determine if replenishment of card supply is needed on a quarterly basis. C. The SA will send an email to the LA administrative site with a tracking number of the bulk inventory.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective: April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:06.0

FD:06.0 - Texas WIC Card Management WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 2 D. If the LA administrative site determines additional cards are needed, the request with the number of additional cards must be sent to wicebtsupport@hhs.texas.gov. II. Receiving Bulk Card Shipment and Distribution A. The EBT vendor will send bulk Texas WIC Card shipments ordered by the SA to each LA's administrative site for distribution to the WIC clinics. B. Within 3 business days of receipt, the LA administrative site will send an email to confirm the number of sleeves received in the shipment to wicebtsupport@hhs.texas.gov. C. The Texas WIC Cards are ready to be assigned to WIC families upon receipt at the clinic. III. Securing and Reporting Discrepancies During LA Clinic Distributions A. LA administrative site will report any discrepancies in Texas WIC Card shipments that occur during internal LA distribution to Clinic Sites to wicebtsupport@hhs.texas.gov within one business day. 1. Texas WIC Cards reported to SA as lost in transit will be cancelled permanently. 2. If the cancelled cards are later found by the LA, they must be discarded according to parent agency protocol. B. The LA administrative site and WIC clinics must keep the Texas WIC Cards secured in a locked area.

body:
Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:10.0

FD:10.0 – Issuing Food Packages for the Mother/Infant Dyad WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 1 Issuing Food Packages for the Mother/Infant Dyad Purpose To establish procedures for issuing food packages to the Mother/Infant dyad. Authority State Policy Policy Mother and infant packages must be prescribed according to the amount the mother is breastfeeding or the amount of formula provided. Packages must be prescribed by a Certifying Authority (CA) or WIC Certification Specialist (WCS). Definitions Electronic Benefit Account (EBA) - the account where food benefits are being held for redemption. Procedures I. When issuing mother/infant food packages, local agency (LA) staff must explain the differences in food package benefits among each of the eligible food packages. A woman may indicate her preference for and be allowed to change to a food package that best suits her needs. Refer to FD:12.0 Food Packages for food package descriptions and FD:12.1 Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges for procedures for exchanging food packages. II. Staff must assess breastfeeding status of breastfeeding infant participants at time of each issuance. If the infant is no longer breastfeeding, staff must enter the date breastfeeding ended and update the infant breastfeeding frequency on the infant's participant page prior to issuance.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:10.0

FD:10.0 – Issuing Food Packages for the Mother/Infant Dyad WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 2 III. Breastfeeding A. Fully Breastfeeding – For a breastfeeding woman, whose infant(s) does not receive any infant formula from WIC (assumed to be fully breastfeeding their infants) B. Partially Breastfeeding- For a partially breastfeeding woman, whose infant(s) receive formula from WIC in amounts that do not exceed the maximum allowance for the partial food packages. 1. This package is available in the birth month, however, staff should encourage women who are mostly breastfeeding to take the Fully Breastfeeding package. 2. The infant will receive up to approximately a half package of formula. 3. Every effort must be made to promote breastfeeding. Staff must encourage and support breastfeeding and use positive language when discussing breastfeeding. A breastfeeding woman who chooses the “Partially” breastfeeding food package in the birth month should be counseled according to Policy BF 1.0. C. Some Breastfeeding – for a woman up to six months postpartum whose infant(s) receives more than the maximum amount of formula allowed for partially breastfed infants. 1. The infant must receive a formula package that is customized to reflect the quantity of formula needed as determined by the Certifying Authority (CA) or the WIC Certification Specialist (WCS) after discussing with the mother and estimating the needs of the infant. The CA or WCS will issue up to the maximum amount of formula allowed and must not automatically issue the maximum amount. 2. Every effort must be made to encourage and support breastfeeding. A breastfeeding woman who chooses the “Some” Breastfeeding food package in the birth month should be provided extra breastfeeding support and encouraged to choose

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:10.0

FD:10.0 – Issuing Food Packages for the Mother/Infant Dyad WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 3 the Fully or Partially Breastfeeding Food Package for advanced issuance months. 3. A breastfed infant who receives less than the maximum amount of formula at initial issuance during the birth month may return to the clinic to receive up to the maximum amount of formula within that month. For example, if 5 cans of powder formula are uploaded to the economic unit’s EBA, the breastfeeding woman can return within the same month to receive the maximum amount allowed of formula. 4. The participant who is receiving the Some Breastfeeding Food Package is no longer eligible to receive WIC foods when she is six months postpartum but does continue to receive breastfeeding support including peer or lactation consultant counseling, breast pumps and participant-centered nutrition education, up to one year postpartum. D. When a breastfeeding woman requests formula or an increase in the amount of formula she receives, staff must: 1. Provide breastfeeding counseling according to BF:01.0 Breastfeeding Promotion and Support Standards Procedure III. D. 2. Inform the woman that she will not be eligible to receive any food benefits after six months postpartum with the "Some" breastfeeding package but will be eligible to receive breastfeeding support. IV. Non-breastfeeding Postpartum A. The Postpartum food package is for women up to six months postpartum who are not breastfeeding their infants. B. The infant must receive the appropriate formula package determined by the CA or the WCS. V. Situations involving a non-birth woman who is providing breastmilk, surrogacy, or a woman whose infant is adopted.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:10.0

FD:10.0 – Issuing Food Packages for the Mother/Infant Dyad WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 4 A. There can be only one breastfeeding woman per WIC infant B. A non-birth woman providing breastmilk to a WIC infant may qualify as a breastfeeding woman, for example an adoptive mother. C. If an adoptive mother is providing breastmilk to the infant, the adoptive mother and the infant will be the dyad in the MIS. The infant will not receive a food package unless the adoptive family qualifies and enrolls the infant in WIC. D. If a surrogate or a mother whose infant is adopted by another family expresses her breastmilk and provides the milk to the WIC infant: 1. She must be certified as a breastfeeding woman and issued the appropriate breastfeeding food package. 2. She will not be linked to the infant in the MIS. E. If a surrogate or a mother whose infant was adopted by another family provides breastmilk to a milk bank, she must be certified as a postpartum woman if it has been less than 6 months since delivery. F. Local agencies may contact the state agency for additional guidance in these situations.

body:
Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective April 1, 2026 Policy No. FD:12.0

FD:12.0 – Food Packages 1 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

Food Packages Purpose To establish procedures for the issuance of allowable foods within the food packages. To ensure food benefits are appropriate for each participant’s health and nutritional needs. Authority 7 CFR 246.10; 26 TAC 366.21 Policy Food packages must be prescribed by a Certifying Authority (CA) or WIC Certification Specialist (WCS). Monthly food benefits are valid for one calendar month, the first day of the month through the last day of that same month. Full food package benefits will be issued to participants on or before the 15th day of the month; partial food package benefits will be issued to participants obtaining food benefits on or after the 16th day of the current month. Formula issuance will be prorated every 10 days for the current month based on the number of days remaining in the month. Participants shall only receive those foods allowed in their participant profile, and their dietary needs and food preparation/storage needs. Definitions Electronic Benefits Account (EBA) – the account where food benefits are being held for redemption. Upload/Load benefits to EBA – benefits are uploaded to the EBA, instead of being written to the card. Procedures I. Food packages must be prescribed by the CA or WCS in consultation with the participant and registered dietitian (RD) when necessary. The

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective April 1, 2026 Policy No. FD:12.0

FD:12.0 – Food Packages 2 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

food package must accommodate the individual’s age, dietary needs, medical/nutritional conditions, and living conditions. II. All food package changes are the responsibility of a CA or WCS. For WCS, refer to Policy FD:13.0 Issuance of Contract Infant Formula, FD:16.0 Approval of Non-Contract Formulas, FD:16.1 Issuance of Formula Food Packages and Transfer Scenarios and FD:19.0 Managing Returned Formula for further instructions regarding food package changes which include formula. III. Individual participant food package benefits will be uploaded to the economic unit’s electronic benefit account (EBA). After all family members’ food packages are uploaded to the economic unit’s EBA, staff must: A. Review the shopping list for accuracy of the food package and amount. The LA may be held financially accountable for all improperly redeemed food benefits. B. Offer a copy of the shopping list and inform the client that they can view their food benefits on myWIC. C. Review the shopping list with the client. D. At the first visit, staff must offer a copy of the Texas WIC Shopping Guide and inform the client that they can view the shopping guide on myWIC. IV. Infant Food Packages A. Food packages for the breastfeeding mother and infant dyad are closely tied and must match except when the mother is breastfeeding multiple infants with differing breastfeeding statuses or if the woman is a surrogate or birth mother whose infant is adopted (refer to Policy FD:10.0 Issuing Food Packages for the Mother/Infant Dyad). B. Staff must assess breastfeeding status of breastfeeding infant participants at the time of each issuance. If the infant is no longer

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective April 1, 2026 Policy No. FD:12.0

FD:12.0 – Food Packages 3 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

breastfeeding, staff must enter the date breastfeeding ended and update the infant breastfeeding frequency on the infant's participant page prior to issuance. C. The parent/guardian can choose between four infant food packages including: 1. Fully breastfeeding – for infants who are breastfed and do not receive infant formula from WIC. 2. Partially breastfeeding – for infants who are breastfed and receive approximately a half package or less of infant formula. 3. Some breastfeeding - for infants who are breastfed at least one time a day and receive greater than a half package of infant formula. 4. Fully formula fed – for infants who are fully formula fed. D. The parent/guardian of an infant 6-11 months of age may choose a fruit and vegetable cash value benefit (CVB) in place of all or some containers of infant fruits and/or vegetables after an individual nutrition assessment. Refer to FD:12.1 Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges for instructions. V. Child Food Packages A. Children under two years of age receive a food package with whole milk (buttermilk is not an option). B. Children two through four years of age receive a food package with fat-free, low-fat milk and/or low-fat buttermilk. VI. Pregnant Women Food Packages A. Women with singleton (one infant) pregnancies must receive the Pregnant woman food package. B. Women who are pregnant with multiples receive the Pregnant with Multiples food package.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective April 1, 2026 Policy No. FD:12.0

FD:12.0 – Food Packages 4 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

C. Pregnant women who are partially breastfeeding singleton infants receive the Pregnant Partially Breastfeeding (PBF) package. D. Pregnant women who are fully breastfeeding singleton infants must receive the Pregnant Fully Breastfeeding (FBF) package. VII. Fully Breastfeeding Women Food Packages The Fully Breastfeeding (FBF) food package may be issued to a breastfeeding mother in any month during which the participant’s infant receives no formula up to the infant’s first birthday. A. When a Fully Breastfeeding food package has been issued and the parent/guardian returns to the clinic to request formula for the infant: 1. If some benefits have not been redeemed and her food package has enough remaining foods to complete the replacement food package, staff must perform a food package exchange and replace for the mother’s food package and issue a formula package to the infant for current and future months. 2. If there are not enough benefits to exchange her food package, the mother is not eligible for a food package exchange for the current month and the infant is not eligible for a formula package. Refer the mother to the local agency peer counselor, designated breastfeeding expert, lactation consultant or other staff trained in lactation management for support maintaining lactation and/or local resources for formula. B. A breastfeeding woman of multiple births from the same pregnancy (e.g., twins, triplets) is eligible to receive the Partially Breastfeeding Multiples food package in the following situations: 1. One infant is not receiving formula from WIC. 2. Two infants are partially breastfeeding. 3. One infant is partially breastfeeding and another infant is some breastfeeding.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective April 1, 2026 Policy No. FD:12.0

FD:12.0 – Food Packages 5 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

C. A breastfeeding woman who has multiple infants from the same pregnancy is eligible to receive the Fully Breastfeeding Multiples package (which is equivalent to 1.5 times the Fully Breastfeeding Package) if two infants are not receiving formula from WIC. VIII. Partially Breastfeeding Women Food Packages A. When a Partially Breastfeeding food package has been issued with less than the partial maximum amount of formula and the mother returns to request additional formula for the infant within the current benefit period, follow the procedures below. If the request is to increase, staff may increase up to the Partial Max at issuance. B. Up to the full formula package: 1. Provide breastfeeding counseling according to Policy BF:01.0 Breastfeeding Promotion and Support Standards Procedure C. 2. Inform the woman that if she chooses to continue breastfeeding at least one time a day but prefers to receive a full package of formula for her infant, she will not be eligible to receive food benefits after the infant turns six month of age but will be eligible to receive breastfeeding support. 3. If the woman still desires an increase in formula, staff ensure the woman’s current food package can be voided and replaced in the MIS. IX. Some Breastfeeding Women Food Packages The Some Breastfeeding profile allows a woman to receive food benefits up to the last day of the month that the infant turns six months. A. The participant is no longer eligible to receive a food package when she is six months postpartum but does continue to receive breastfeeding support including peer or lactation consultant counseling, breast pumps and participant-centered nutrition education, up to one year postpartum.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective April 1, 2026 Policy No. FD:12.0

FD:12.0 – Food Packages 6 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

B. If certified after six months postpartum, the participant should be encouraged to utilize WIC services, although she will not receive food benefits. X. Postpartum Women Food Packages Postpartum women who are not breastfeeding and whose infants are receiving a full formula package are issued the Postpartum food package for up to the last day of the month the infant turns six months. XI. Other Food Package Types A. Limited or No Refrigeration food package may be issued to participants when there is a lack of food storage or food preparation facilities. 1. The food package provides peanut butter and/or canned beans as a substitute for eggs. 2. Dry powder milk is provided and the package excludes cheese and yogurt. B. Lactose-free milk food packages can be issued by request to women and children. Participants may report lactose intolerance diagnosed by a physician, describe symptoms of lactose intolerance (nausea, gas, diarrhea, abdominal bloating or cramps) when dairy products are consumed or prefer lactose-free milk. Medical documentation is not required for lactose-free milk. C. Soy milk food packages can be issued by request for women and children. Reasons for issuing include, but are not limited to: milk allergy, lactose intolerance, galactosemia, vegan diet and cultural practices. Medical documentation is not required for soy milk. D. Low-fat milk (1% or fat-free milk) is available to children under two years of age for overweight, obesity or for other medical conditions such as fatty acid deficiency that is self-reported by parent/guardian/caretaker or as reported by a healthcare provider

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission Effective April 1, 2026 Policy No. FD:12.0

FD:12.0 – Food Packages 7 WIC Policy and Procedures Manual

or registered dietitian (RD). Low-fat milk can be issued by substitution in place of whole milk in the standard food package. 1. A CA or WCS, after consultation with the parent/guardian/caretaker and/or HCP if necessary can make a determination for the need for low-fat milk based on the complete nutrition assessment (e.g., dietary intake, risk code assignment, etc.). 2. A CA can approve low-fat milk for medical reasons in consultation with healthcare provider if necessary. If self- reported by a parent/guardian/caretaker, an RD must approve. XII. Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges. A. Food item substitutions can be made to meet participants’ medical needs, cultural eating patterns, or food preferences. Food packages can be tailored or exchanged to meet participants’ needs. See FD:12.1 Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges. XIII. Issuing Packages with Formula A. For special dietary needs food packages with formula for woman and children, refer to Policy FD:16.1 Issuance of Formula Food Packages and Transfer Scenarios. B. For food packages with formula, the current month formula issuances will be prorated, except for issuances on the first day of the month. The quantity of formula issued by the MIS will be prorated every 10 days for the current month. C. Children and women may be issued up to a full quantity of formula. Lower quantities may be issued if specified by the healthcare provider on the Texas WIC Medical Request for Formula/Food or Texas WIC Medical Request for Metabolic Formula/Food form or by parent/guardian request. body:
FD 12.1 – Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 1 Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:12.1

Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges Purpose To allow for food package substitutions, tailoring, and exchanges. Authority CFR 246.10 Policy Food item substitutions can be made to meet participants’ medical needs, cultural eating patterns, or food preferences. Food packages can be tailored or exchanged to meet participants’ needs. These changes must be made by a Certifying Authority (CA) or WIC Certification Specialist (WCS). Definitions Electronic Benefit Account (EBA) - the account where participant food benefits are being held for redemption. Procedures I. Substitutions in Food Packages A. Food item substitutions can be made in the milk, cereal, and fruit and vegetable food groups to better meet the participants’ needs and preferences. Available substitutions may vary per category. B. Milk Substitution Group 1. Substitutions can be made within children’s and women’s food packages, per participant’s preference, for different types of milk (e.g., milk and evaporated milk) based on quart equivalents. 2. Milk substitutions include: a. Milk, lactose-free milk, and soy milk – one quart is

FD 12.1 – Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 2 Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:12.1

one quart equivalent b. Pea protein milk – two 48-ounce containers is three quarts equivalent c. Dry milk – 3.2 ounces is one quart equivalent d. Evaporated milk – 16 fluid ounces is one quart equivalent (1:2 ratio) e. Cheese – one pound is three quarts equivalent f. Tofu – One pound (16 ounces) is one quart equivalent g. Yogurt – one quart (32 ounces) is one quart equivalent 3. Cheese - Food packages cannot contain more than one pound of cheese with the exception of: Fully Breastfeeding, Fully Breastfeeding and Pregnant, Partially Breastfeeding and Pregnant, Pregnant with Multiples, Fully Breastfeeding Multiples, and Partially Breastfeeding Multiples food packages, which can contain a maximum of 2 pounds of. cheese. 4. Yogurt a. Food packages cannot contain more than two quarts of yogurt. b. One pound (16 ounces) of tofu can be substituted for one quart of yogurt. 5. Tofu – Tofu can be issued up to the full fluid milk equivalence for reasons such as milk allergy, lactose intolerance and vegan diets. 6. Kosher milk and cheese are available for participants who must consume kosher foods due to religious eating patterns. Documentation is not required. Kosher milk and cheese can be issued by substitution in place of milk and cheese in the standard food package. Another option for participants who need to keep kosher is soy milk and tofu as soy milk is pareve (can be eaten with both meat and dairy dishes).

FD 12.1 – Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 3 Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:12.1

C. Cereal Substitution Group – Infant cereal can be substituted for breakfast cereal in women’s and children’s Special Dietary Needs food packages only. To receive this food package, staff must obtain a Texas WIC Medical Request form from the client’s Health Care Provider. D. Fruit and Vegetable Substitution Group – 1. One juice item (64-ounce bottle or 16-ounce frozen juice) can be substituted for some of the fruit and vegetable cash value benefit (CVB) per participant’s preference. 2. In women’s and children’s Special Dietary Needs food packages, jarred infant food fruits and/or vegetables can be substituted for fruit and vegetable cash value benefit (CVB). To receive this food package, staff must obtain a Texas WIC Medical Request form from the client’s Health Care Provider. II. Tailoring Food Packages A. Individual nutrition tailoring is allowed based on the CA or WCS’ assessment of a participant’s supplemental nutrition needs. B. The full maximum monthly allowance of all supplemental foods in all food packages should be made available to participants unless medically or nutritionally warranted. C. Tailoring the package to provide less than the full amount is appropriate when, for example: 1. It is medically or nutritionally warranted such as removing an item due to a food allergy. 2. When a participant refuses or cannot use the maximum monthly amount. D. Food packages for women and children 1-5 can be tailored to include sunflower seed butter as an additional option for the beans and peanut butter food item.

FD 12.1 – Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 4 Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:12.1

1. If clients prefer sunflower seed butter based on dietary needs, client preference, cultural practices, etc., the issuing CA or WCS will inform the client that they can get sunflower seed butter with their “beans or peanut butter” benefit. 2. No changes to the food package are required in the MIS. 3. Medical documentation is not required.

E. The parent/guardian of an infant 6-11 months of age may choose a fruit and vegetable cash value benefit (CVB) in place of all or some containers of infant fruits and/or vegetables after an individual nutrition assessment. 1. A CA or WCS must individually assess caregiver preference prior to issuing a food package with an infant CVB. 2. When issuing a food package with an infant CVB, the CA or WCS must provide appropriate nutrition education on safe food preparation, storage techniques and feeding practices. a. This can be accomplished by providing Preparing Fruits and Vegetables for Your Baby (stock no. 13-06-16828) or web-based resources. b. Examples of documentation in the MIS may include but are not limited to a nutrition note during the midpoint or NE appointment, proof of appropriate NE or a record of sending a digital resource. 3. The parent/guardian of an infant 6-11 months of age may select one of the following food package options: a. Maximum amount (32 4-ounce containers) of infant fruits and/or vegetables (default issuance) b. Maximum infant CVB c. Half the amount (16 4-ounce containers) of infant fruits and/or vegetables and half the infant CVB

III. Food Package Exchanges

FD 12.1 – Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 5 Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:12.1

A. Food packages can be exchanged in the current month by modifying benefits if the remaining benefits meet the following criteria: 1. The quantities of each food are equal to or more than the quantity in the original food package, and 2. The types of foods are the same as in the original food package, or if not the same, the food has not been redeemed. a. Items within the milk substitution group described in I.B.2 are considered the same type of food and can be exchanged as available to that participant category. i. Example 1: A pregnant participant wants to exchange her regular low-fat milk for low-fat lactose-free milk. Staff may exchange the regular low-fat milk for low-fat lactose-free milk, even if the regular low-fat milk was partially redeemed. ii. Example 2: A 3-year-old child received low-fat milk, but then their caregiver obtains a prescription for a nutritional supplement, so the child is eligible to receive whole milk. Staff may exchange the low-fat milk for whole milk even if the low-fat milk was partially redeemed. b. Infant 6-11 month food packages can be exchanged if less than half of the containers of infant fruits and/or vegetables have been redeemed. Staff may exchange 16 of the remaining containers for half of the infant CVB amount after an individual assessment as described in II. D. c. A food package exchange may not be possible if foods from the first package were redeemed in an amount that exceeds the amount in the newly requested food package. For example - a Fully Breastfeeding Package with all 20 ounces of canned fish already redeemed cannot be exchanged for a Postpartum Package because that only contains 10 ounces of canned fish. B. Formula Food Package Exchanges

FD 12.1 – Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 6 Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:12.1

1. Formula to Formula a. Any formula food package can be exchanged for another formula food package at any time if the formula quantity in the economic unit’s Electronic Benefit Account (EBA) and/or quantity returned is equal to or more than the formula quantity in the new food package. b. When exchanging food packages with formula, formula will not be prorated for the current month. c. When a Partially Breastfeeding food package has been issued with less than the partial maximum amount of formula and the mother returns to request additional formula within the current benefit period, follow the procedures below: i. Staff may increase up to the partial maximum without a change in the Mother’s food package. ii. To increase to full formula package: a) Provide breastfeeding counseling according to Policy BF:01.0 Breastfeeding Promotion and Support Standards, Procedure III.D. b) Inform the woman that if she chooses to continue breastfeeding at least one time a day but prefers to receive a full package of formula for her infant, she will not be eligible to receive food benefits after the infant turns six months of age, but will be eligible to receive breastfeeding support. c) If the woman still desires an increase in formula, staff must verify that the woman’s current food package can be modified in the MIS. 2. Formula to Non-Formula - a formula food package can be exchanged for non-formula food package if the amount of formula originally issued either remains in the economic

FD 12.1 – Food Package Substitutions, Tailoring and Exchanges WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 7 Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective April 1, 2026

Policy No. FD:12.1

unit’s EBA and/or the unopened formula containers are returned to clinic. 3. Non-formula to Formula – When a non-formula food package is exchanged for a formula food package, the quantity of food originally issued must be equal or more than the quantity of food in the new food package. 4. Fully Breastfeeding to Formula – a. When a Fully Breastfeeding food package has been issued and the mother returns for formula before her infant turns six months, the food package can be exchanged in the current month if the remaining benefits quantities of each food are equal to or more than the quantity in the original food package, and b. Staff may then perform a food package exchange and modify benefits for the mother’s food package and issue a formula package to the infant for current and future months. See Policy FD:10.0 Issuing Food Packages for the Mother/Infant Dyad for more information. c. If there are not enough remaining benefits for the current month: i. A food package exchange cannot be performed. ii. Refer the mother to the local agency peer counselor or lactation consultant and/or local resources for formula.

body:
Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective August 1, 2022

Policy No. FD:13.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 1 Issuance of Contract Infant Formula Purpose To ensure that participants needing milk-based and soy-based infant formula receive contract formula. Authority 7 CFR 246.2; 7 CFR 246.10 Policy In instances when breastfeeding is medically contraindicated or when a parent requests formula, contract formula may be issued. Contract brand infant formula must be issued as the first choice unless an exempt/WIC eligible nutritional has been prescribed by a health care professional licensed to write prescriptions under state law for a qualifying condition(s). Contract brand infant formula may only be issued to participants older than one year of age when prescribed by a health care professional for a qualifying condition(s). Only Certifying authorities or WIC Certification Specialists (WCS) may assign contract formula. Definitions Alternate contract infant formula – any contract brand, non-exempt infant formula, other than the primary contract infant formula that is subject to rebate under cost containment procedures. Contract brand infant formula - all infant formulas (except exempt infant formulas) produced by the manufacturer awarded the infant formula cost containment contract.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective August 1, 2022

Policy No. FD:13.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 2 Formula – the term formula used throughout this policy refers to all contract and non-contract formulas, including milk and soy-based, low- lactose formulas, nutritional beverages, additives such as human milk fortifiers and modular products, nutritional supplements and WIC-eligible nutritionals. Exempt infant formula – therapeutic formula intended and labeled for use by individuals with specific medical and/or dietary conditions. Primary contract infant formula — the specific infant formula for which manufacturers submit a bid to a State agency in response to a rebate solicitation and for which a contract is awarded by the State agency as a result of that bid. WIC - eligible nutritionals – certain enteral products that are specifically formulated to provide nutritional support for individuals with a qualifying condition, when the use of conventional foods is precluded, restricted or inadequate. Such WIC eligible nutritionals must serve the purpose of a food, meal or diet (may be nutritionally complete or incomplete) and provide a source of calories and one or more nutrients, be designed for enteral digestions via an oral or tube feeding (e.g. Pediasure) and may not be a conventional food, drug, flavoring or enzyme. Procedures I. Contract milk-based infant formula a. Issue the primary milk-based contract infant formula unless: i. The infant is already taking an alternate contract milk-based or soy-based infant formula and the parent/guardian wants to continue that formula or; ii. The infant is already taking another manufacturer’s product that is comparable to the alternate contract milk- or soy-based infant formula. Staff may offer the contract product that is most comparable – the infant does not have to trial the primary milk-based formula first.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective August 1, 2022

Policy No. FD:13.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 3 iii. A caregiver requests an alternate milk or soy-based contract infant formula or; iv. The CA determines, using professional judgement, that an alternate contract infant formula may better meet the infant’s feeding needs. v. The caregiver presents a medical request from the health care professional for a non-contract formula that can be approved and issued per policy FD:16.0. II. Contract soy-based infant formula a. Issue the contract soy-based infant formula in cases where: i. The family follows a vegan (vegetarian, no dairy) diet and requires a soy formula or; ii. There is a family preference and/or caregiver request for soy formula or; iii. There is a medical request from a healthcare professional for a soy-based formula. III. When a caregiver requests a change in contract formula due to symptoms of reported intolerance, the CA or WCS should: a. Assess and counsel prior to making a formula change. i. Explore the feeding, preparation and/or storage practices. Provide appropriate counseling and education. Refer to health care professional as needed. ii. If the caregiver reports symptoms of: Diarrhea, bloody stools, vomiting, fever, weight loss, poor or no weight gain, make a referral to the infant’s health care professional. Document the referral in the participant’s record. b. Document the reason for the contract formula change and symptoms experienced in Notes section of the participant page. IV. Issuance of contract infant formula to a participant older than one year of age:

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective August 1, 2022

Policy No. FD:13.0

WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 4 a. Obtain a medical request from the health care professional and complete an assessment and appropriate documentation for approval. b. Assessment includes a diet history, anthropometric measurement and any relevant medical history. V. Concentrating (or altering the standard dilution) of contract infant formula: a. Issue only up to the maximum amount of formula as outlined in the Maximum Quantity tables. Quantities cannot be increased to offset reduced final volume that results from concentration. b. Provide instruction for mixing formula to concentrations other than the standard dilution only with a written or verbal request from the health care professional. i. Mixing instructions for concentrating contract formulas to 22, 24, 27 and 30 kcal/oz can be requested from the state agency. ii. It is not necessary to contact the state office for approval to provide mixing instructions for contract formula. iii. Document verbal requests from healthcare providers in VENA notes. Include name and contact information of healthcare provider, date of request and reason for increased calorie need. iv. Scan and upload written requests to the client record in the MIS. VI. Formula only food package issuance a. The special needs food package for infants 6 months of age and older may be issued with contract formula. b. Obtain a medical request from the HCP indicating foods are to be omitted due to an inability or delay in consuming solids. VII. In the event that a contract formula does not meet federal regulations, a medical request from a prescribing authority will be required.

body:
Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective June 1, 2024

Policy No. FD:15.0

FD:15.0 – Issuance of Ready-to-Use Formula WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 1 Issuance of Ready-to-Use Formula Purpose To ensure the availability of ready-to-use formula (RTU) to WIC participants with specific needs. Authority 7 CFR Part 246.10 Policy Formula will be issued in concentrated liquid or powder form unless the participant’s circumstances meet the criteria for ready-to-use formula issuance outlined in this policy as determined by a certification authority (CA). Procedures I. RTU formula will only be issued due to one or more of the following conditions: A. The participant’s household has an unsafe, unsanitary or limited water supply, or poor refrigeration; B. The parent/caretaker or participant is unable to correctly dilute or prepare formula; C. The formula is available only in a RTU form. 1. Formula manufactured only in RTU form should be issued as RTU for the full length of approval. 2. Local agency staff should refer to the state agency for guidance on the appropriate length of issuance for formula that is temporarily unavailable in powder or concentrate form, such as in the event of a shortage or recall.

Texas WIC Health and Human Services Commission

Effective June 1, 2024

Policy No. FD:15.0

FD:15.0 – Issuance of Ready-to-Use Formula WIC Policy and Procedures Manual 2 D. The use of RTU therapeutic formula for infants, and any formula for women and children, better accommodates a participant’s condition (e.g., compromised immune system). Refer to the specific formula in the Texas WIC Formulary; or E. The use of RTU therapeutic formula for infants, and any formula for women and children, improves a participant’s compliance in consuming the prescribed formula. Refer to the specific formula in the Texas WIC Formulary. II. The continued issuance of RTU must be evaluated at each formula approval for therapeutic formulas and each time formula benefits are issued for contract formulas. III. When issuing RTU formula, a CA must document the reason for issuance in the participant’s record.
